requirements.text: The web application should provide a 'Student Grade Book' interface where users can add student details. The interface must include a form with a 'Student Name' input field (data-testid: 'student-name') and a 'Grade (0-100)' input field (data-testid: 'student-grade'), both of which are required. The grade input should accept numeric values between 0 and 100, inclusive. A submit button labeled 'Add Student' (data-testid: 'add-student-button') should be present to submit the form. Upon clicking the 'Add Student' button, if the inputs are valid, the student's name and grade should be appended to a list (data-testid: 'student-list') as a new list item with a unique data-id attribute. The form fields should then be reset to empty. If the grade is outside the 0-100 range, the system should prevent submission, display an error message indicating the valid range, and retain the entered values in the input fields. The system should handle normal cases, edge cases (minimum and maximum grades), and error scenarios (invalid grades) as described.

The system must validate form submissions on the 'Student Grade Book' page to ensure data integrity. Specifically: 1) The 'Student Name' input field (identified by data-testid='student-name') must not be empty. 2) The 'Grade (0-100)' input field (identified by data-testid='student-grade') must contain a numeric value within the inclusive range of 0 to 100. If either condition is violated, the form submission should be blocked, and no new student entry should be added to the student list (identified by data-testid='student-list'). Upon successful validation, the form submission should add a new list item to the student list, displaying the student's name and grade in the format 'Name: Grade'. Each list item must have a unique data-id attribute in the format 'student-item-{index}', where {index} is the 1-based position of the student in the list. The form (identified by data-testid='student-form') should reset after a successful submission. The system must handle edge cases, including grades at the boundaries (0 and 100), and prevent submission for grades below 0 or above 100. All interactions should be performed using the specified data-testid attributes for consistency and testability.

The web application 'Student Grade Book' must allow users to add students with their respective grades using a form. The form consists of an input field for the student's name (data-testid: 'student-name') and an input field for the student's grade (data-testid: 'student-grade'), which accepts numeric values between 0 and 100 inclusive. Upon clicking the 'Add Student' button (data-testid: 'add-student-button'), the system should validate the inputs. If the inputs are valid, the student's name and grade should be added to the student list (data-testid: 'student-list'), displayed as a list item with a unique data-id attribute. After successfully adding a student, the input fields should be cleared to allow for new entries. If the grade input is invalid (e.g., not within the 0-100 range), the student should not be added to the list, and the input fields should retain their values for correction. The system should ensure consistent use of data-testid attributes for accessing and manipulating DOM elements.

generated_cases.description: Leave the student name field empty while providing a valid grade. Click the 'Add Student' button and verify that the form submission is blocked and no entry is added to the list.

generated_cases.description: Enter a valid student name and the minimum boundary grade of 0 in the grade input field, then click the 'Add Student' button. Verify that the student is successfully added to the student list and the form fields are reset.

generated_cases.title: Add student with maximum valid grade boundary (100)
generated_cases.description: Enter a valid student name and the maximum boundary grade of 100 in the grade input field, then click the 'Add Student' button. Verify that the student is successfully added to the student list and the form fields are reset.

generated_cases.description: Enter a valid student name and an invalid grade of -1 (just below the minimum boundary) in the grade input field, then click the 'Add Student' button. Verify that submission is prevented, an error message is displayed, no entry is added to the student list, and the input values are retained.

generated_cases.title: Attempt to add student with grade just above maximum (101)
generated_cases.description: Enter a valid student name and an invalid grade of 101 (just above the maximum boundary) in the grade input field, then click the 'Add Student' button. Verify that submission is prevented, an error message is displayed, no entry is added to the student list, and the input values are retained.

generated_cases.title: Add student with a typical normal internal value (50)
generated_cases.description: Enter a valid student name and a nominal internal grade of 50 in the grade input field, then click the 'Add Student' button. Verify that the student is successfully added to the list and the form resets.

generated_cases.title: Successful Addition of Student with Valid Grade
generated_cases.description: Navigate to the Student Grade Book interface, enter a valid student name in 'student-name', enter a valid grade within 0-100 in 'student-grade', and click 'add-student-button'. Verify that the student is added to 'student-list' in the format 'Name: Grade' with a unique data-id attribute ('student-item-1') and the form fields are reset to empty.

generated_cases.title: Edge Case Addition of Students at Grade Boundaries
generated_cases.description: Perform two separate submissions in the Student Grade Book interface: first with grade 0 and second with grade 100 alongside valid student names. Verify that both boundary values are accepted, added successfully to 'student-list' with unique data-id attributes, and the form resets correctly.

generated_cases.title: Abnormal Submission with Invalid Grade Outside 0-100 Range
generated_cases.description: Enter a student name and an invalid grade (e.g., -1 or 101) into 'student-grade' in the Student Grade Book interface, then click 'add-student-button'. Verify that the submission is prevented, an error message indicating the valid range is displayed, the student is not added to 'student-list', and the input fields retain their entered values.

generated_cases.title: Abnormal Submission with Empty Student Name
generated_cases.description: Leave the 'student-name' input field empty while entering a valid grade in 'student-grade', then click 'add-student-button'. Verify that form submission is blocked, no new entry is appended to 'student-list', and data integrity is maintained.

generated_cases.title: Submit Form With Grade Below Minimum Range
generated_cases.description: Attempt to submit the student grade book form with a grade value of -1 to verify that the system blocks submission, displays an error message, and retains the entered values.

generated_cases.title: Submit Form With Grade Above Maximum Range
generated_cases.description: Attempt to submit the student grade book form with a grade value of 101 to verify that the system blocks submission, displays an error message, and retains the entered values.

generated_cases.description: Attempt to submit the student grade book form with a valid grade but an empty student name field to verify that validation blocks the entry and prevents list modification.

technique_rationales.equivalence_partitioning: Partition valid and invalid classes for student name and grade inputs (e.g., valid names vs empty names, valid grades 0-100 vs invalid grades below 0 or above 100).
technique_rationales.boundary_value_analysis: Exercise grade limits and boundaries explicitly mentioned in the requirements, specifically at 0, 100, and immediately outside the limits such as -1 and 101.
technique_rationales.use_case: Cover the end-to-end user flow of filling out the student grade book form, submitting valid data, appending to the student list, and resetting the form.
technique_rationales.error_guessing: Explore plausible user errors and failure conditions such as submitting empty fields or out-of-range grades, verifying that submission is blocked and values are retained.
